adhovīkṣaṇaśīlaṃ ca samyagdṛṣṭisamanvitam // 61
32.d:
साहसानुप्रवेशेन कुञ्चितं हस्तयुग्मकम् ।
अधोवीक्षणशीलं च सम्यग्दृष्टिसमन्वितम् ॥ 61
32.m:
with both hands contracted by a bold entry,
endowed with a downward looking and an even gaze:

32.s:
vīrabhairavasaṃjñeyaṃ khecarī bodhavardhinī /
aṣṭadhetthaṃ varṇitā śrībhargāṣṭakaśikhākule // 62
32.d:
वीरभैरवसंज्ञेयं खेचरी बोधवर्धिनी ।
अष्टधेत्थं वर्णिता श्रीभर्गाष्टकशिखाकुले ॥ 62
32.m:
this Khecarī, known as Vīrabhairavā, increases awakening.
Thus it has been described in eight ways in the family of the Śrībhargāṣṭakaśikhā.

32.s:
evaṃ nānāvidhānbhedānāśrityaikaiva yā sthitā /
śrīkhecarī tayāviṣṭaḥ paraṃ bījaṃ prapadyate // 63
32.d:
एवं नानाविधान्भेदानाश्रित्यैकैव या स्थिता ।
श्रीखेचरी तयाविष्टः परं बीजं प्रपद्यते ॥ 63
32.m:
Thus, resorting to diverse divisions, she who abides as one alone,
the venerable Khecarī—possessed by her, one attains the supreme seed-syllable.

32.s:
ekaṃ sṛṣṭimayaṃ bījaṃ yadvīryaṃ sarvamantragam /
ekā mudrā khecarī ca mudraughaḥ prāṇito yayā // 64
32.d:
एकं सृष्टिमयं बीजं यद्वीर्यं सर्वमन्त्रगम् ।
एका मुद्रा खेचरी च मुद्रौघः प्राणितो यया ॥ 64
32.m:
The one seed-syllable composed of emission is the potency residing in all mantras;
and the one mudrā is Khecarī, by which the flood of mudrās is enlivened.

32.s:
tadevaṃ khecarīcakrarūḍhau yadrūpamullaset /
tadeva mudrā mantavyā śeṣaḥ syāddehavikriyā // 65
32.d:
तदेवं खेचरीचक्ररूढौ यद्रूपमुल्लसेत् ।
तदेव मुद्रा मन्तव्या शेषः स्याद्देहविक्रिया ॥ 65
32.m:
Therefore, whatever form shines forth when ascending the cakra of Khecarī,
that alone should be considered the mudrā; the rest is merely bodily distortion.

32.s:
yāgādau tanmadhye tadavasitau jñānayogaparimarśe /
vighnapraśame pāśacchede mudrāvidheḥ samayaḥ // 66
32.d:
यागादौ तन्मध्ये तदवसितौ ज्ञानयोगपरिमर्शे ।
विघ्नप्रशमे पाशच्छेदे मुद्राविधेः समयः ॥ 66
32.m:
At the beginning of sacrifice, in its middle, at its conclusion, in reflective contemplation on the yoga of knowledge,
in the quelling of obstacles, [and] in the cutting of bonds is the occasion for the rule of mudrā.

32.s:
bodhāveśaḥ sannidhiraikyena visarjanaṃ svarūpagatiḥ /
śaṅkādalanaṃ cakrodayadīptiriti kramātkṛtyam // 67
iti mudrāvidhiḥ proktaḥ sugūḍho yaḥ phalapradaḥ /
32.d:
बोधावेशः सन्निधिरैक्येन विसर्जनं स्वरूपगतिः ।
शङ्कादलनं चक्रोदयदीप्तिरिति क्रमात्कृत्यम् ॥ 67
इति मुद्राविधिः प्रोक्तः सुगूढो यः फलप्रदः ।
32.m:
Possession by awakening, presence, dismissal through oneness, attainment of one's own nature,
dissolution of doubt, and radiance at the rise of the cakra: such is the function in order.
Thus the rule of mudrā has been declared, which is very secret and bears fruit.

33.s:
athāvasarasaṃprāpta ekīkāro nigadyate /
yaduktaṃ cakrabhedena sārdhaṃ pūjyamiti trikam /
tatraiṣa cakrabhedānāmekīkāro diśānayā // 1
33.d:
अथावसरसंप्राप्त एकीकारो निगद्यते ।
यदुक्तं चक्रभेदेन सार्धं पूज्यमिति त्रिकम् ।
तत्रैष चक्रभेदानामेकीकारो दिशानया ॥ 1
33.m:
Now the unification that has reached its proper turn is set forth:
As it was said that the Trika is to be worshipped together according to the variety of cakras,
there this unification of the varieties of cakras [is explained] in this manner:

33.s:
viśvā tadīśā hāraudrī vīranetryambikā tathā /
gurvīti ṣaḍare devyaḥ śrīsiddhāvīradarśitāḥ // 2
33.d:
विश्वा तदीशा हारौद्री वीरनेत्र्यम्बिका तथा ।
गुर्वीति षडरे देव्यः श्रीसिद्धावीरदर्शिताः ॥ 2
33.m:
Viśvā, Tadīśā, Hāraudrī, Vīranetrī, Ambikā,
and Gurvī: these are the goddesses in the six-spoked [cakra] revealed in the venerable Siddhāvīra.

33.s:
māheśī brāhmaṇī skāndī vaiṣṇavyaindrī yamātmikā /
cāmuṇḍā caiva yogīśītyaṣṭāghoryādayo'thavā // 3
33.d:
माहेशी ब्राह्मणी स्कान्दी वैष्णव्यैन्द्री यमात्मिका ।
चामुण्डा चैव योगीशीत्यष्टाघोर्यादयोऽथवा ॥ 3
33.m:
Māheśī, Brāhmaṇī, Skāndī, Vaiṣṇavī, Aindrī, Yamātmakā,
Cāmuṇḍā, and Yogīśī: [these] eight, or Aghorī and the others,

33.s:
agninirṛtivāyvīśamātṛbhirdvādaśānvitāḥ /
nandā bhadrā jayā kālī karālī vikṛtānanā // 4
33.d:
अग्निनिरृतिवाय्वीशमातृभिर्द्वादशान्विताः ।
नन्दा भद्रा जया काली कराली विकृतानना ॥ 4
33.m:
combined with the mothers of Agni, Nirṛti, Vāyu, and Īśa, are twelve:
Nandā, Bhadrā, Jayā, Kālī, Karālī, Vikṛtānanā,

33.s:
kroṣṭukī bhīmamudrā ca vāyuvegā hayānanā /
gambhīrā ghoṣaṇī ceti caturviṃśatyare vidhiḥ // 5
33.d:
क्रोष्टुकी भीममुद्रा च वायुवेगा हयानना ।
गम्भीरा घोषणी चेति चतुर्विंशत्यरे विधिः ॥ 5
33.m:
Kroṣṭukī, Bhīmamudrā, Vāyuvegā, Hayānanā,
Gambhīrā, and Ghoṣaṇī: such is the rule in the twenty-four-spoked [cakra].

33.s:
siddhirvṛddhirdyutirlakṣmīrmedhā kāntiḥ sudhā dhṛtiḥ /
dīptiḥ puṣṭirmatiḥ kīrtiḥ susthitiḥ sugatiḥ smṛtiḥ // 6
33.d:
सिद्धिर्वृद्धिर्द्युतिर्लक्ष्मीर्मेधा कान्तिः सुधा धृतिः ।
दीप्तिः पुष्टिर्मतिः कीर्तिः सुस्थितिः सुगतिः स्मृतिः ॥ 6
33.m:
Siddhi, Vṛddhi, Dyuti, Lakṣmī, Medhā, Kānti, Sudhā, Dhṛti,
Dīpti, Puṣṭi, Mati, Kīrti, Susthiti, Sugati, Smṛti,

33.s:
suprabhā ṣoḍaśī ceti śrīkaṇṭhādikaśaktayaḥ /
baliśca balinandaśca daśagrīvo haro hayaḥ // 7
33.d:
सुप्रभा षोडशी चेति श्रीकण्ठादिकशक्तयः ।
बलिश्च बलिनन्दश्च दशग्रीवो हरो हयः ॥ 7
33.m:
and Suprabhā as the sixteenth: these are the powers beginning with Śrīkaṇṭha.
Bali, Balinanda, Daśagrīva, Hara, Haya,

33.s:
mādhavaḥ ṣaḍare cakre dvādaśāre tvamī smṛtāḥ /
dakṣaścaṇḍo haraḥ śauṇḍī pramatho bhīmamanmathau // 8
33.d:
माधवः षडरे चक्रे द्वादशारे त्वमी स्मृताः ।
दक्षश्चण्डो हरः शौण्डी प्रमथो भीममन्मथौ ॥ 8
33.m:
and Mādhava are in the six-spoked cakra; in the twelve-spoked, however, these are remembered:
Dakṣa, Caṇḍa, Hara, Śauṇḍī, Pramatha, Bhīma, Manmatha,

33.s:
śakuniḥ sumatirnando gopālaśca pitāmahaḥ /
śrīkaṇṭho'nantasūkṣmau ca trimūrtiḥ śaṃbareśvaraḥ // 9
33.d:
शकुनिः सुमतिर्नन्दो गोपालश्च पितामहः ।
श्रीकण्ठोऽनन्तसूक्ष्मौ च त्रिमूर्तिः शंबरेश्वरः ॥ 9
33.m:
Śakuni, Sumati, Nanda, Gopāla, Pitāmaha,
Śrīkaṇṭha, Ananta, Sūkṣma, Trimūrti, Śaṃbareśvara,

33.s:
arghīśo bhārabhūtiśca sthitiḥ sthāṇurharastathā /
jhaṇṭhibhautikasadyojānugrahakrūrasainikāḥ // 10
33.d:
अर्घीशो भारभूतिश्च स्थितिः स्थाणुर्हरस्तथा ।
झण्ठिभौतिकसद्योजानुग्रहक्रूरसैनिकाः ॥ 10
33.m:
Arghīśa, Bhārabhūti, Sthiti, Sthāṇu, Hara,
Jhaṇṭhi, Bhautika, Sadyojāta, Anugraha, and Krūrasainika.

33.s:
dvyaṣṭau yadvāmṛtastena yuktāḥ pūrṇābhataddravāḥ /
oghormisyandanāṅgāśca vapurudgāravaktrakāḥ // 11
33.d:
द्व्यष्टौ यद्वामृतस्तेन युक्ताः पूर्णाभतद्द्रवाः ।
ओघोर्मिस्यन्दनाङ्गाश्च वपुरुद्गारवक्त्रकाः ॥ 11
33.m:
Twice eight [are these], endowed with the nectar-thief, of full radiance, their liquid
streaming with bodies of billows, their mouths pouring forth bodily form,

33.s:
tanusecanamūrtīśāḥ sarvāmṛtadharo'paraḥ /
śrīpāṭhācchaktayaścaitāḥ ṣoḍaśaiva prakīrtitāḥ // 12
33.d:
तनुसेचनमूर्तीशाः सर्वामृतधरोऽपरः ।
श्रीपाठाच्छक्तयश्चैताः षोडशैव प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 12
33.m:
lords of forms who sprinkle the body; another bears all nectar.
And from the holy reading, these sixteen powers are proclaimed:

33.s:
saṃvartalakulibhṛgusitabakakhaṅgipinākibhujagabalikālāḥ /
dviśchagalāṇḍau śikhiśoṇameṣamīnatridaṇḍi sāṣāḍhi // 13
33.d:
संवर्तलकुलिभृगुसितबकखङ्गिपिनाकिभुजगबलिकालाः ।
द्विश्छगलाण्डौ शिखिशोणमेषमीनत्रिदण्डि साषाढि ॥ 13
33.m:
Saṃvarta, Lakulin, Bhṛgu, Sitabaka, Khaṅgin, Pinākin, Bhujaga, Bali, Kāla,
the two Chagalāṇḍas, Śikhin, Śoṇa, Meṣa, Mīna, Tridaṇḍin, Sāṣāḍhi,

33.s:
devīkāntatadardhau dārukahalisomanāthaśarmāṇaḥ /
jayavijayajayantājitasujayajayarudrakīrtanāvahakāḥ // 14
33.d:
देवीकान्ततदर्धौ दारुकहलिसोमनाथशर्माणः ।
जयविजयजयन्ताजितसुजयजयरुद्रकीर्तनावहकाः ॥ 14
33.m:
Devīkānta, his half, Dāruka, Halin, Somanātha, Śarman,
Jaya, Vijaya, Jayanta, Ajita, Sujaya, Jayarudra, Kīrtanāvahaka,

33.s:
tanmūrtyutsāhadavardhanāśca balasubalabhadradāvahakāḥ /
tadvāndātā ceśo nandanasamabhadratanmūrtiḥ // 15
33.d:
तन्मूर्त्युत्साहदवर्धनाश्च बलसुबलभद्रदावहकाः ।
तद्वान्दाता चेशो नन्दनसमभद्रतन्मूर्तिः ॥ 15
33.m:
Tanmūrtyutsāhadavardhana, Bala, Subala, Bhadradāvahaka,
Tadvāndātṛ, Īśa, Nandana, Samabhadratanmūrti,

33.s:
śivadasumanaḥspṛhaṇakā durgo bhadrākhyakālaśca /
ceto'nugakauśikakālaviśvasuśivāstathāparaḥ kopaḥ // 16
33.d:
शिवदसुमनःस्पृहणका दुर्गो भद्राख्यकालश्च ।
चेतोऽनुगकौशिककालविश्वसुशिवास्तथापरः कोपः ॥ 16
33.m:
Śivada, Sumanaspṛhaṇaka, Durga, and Kāla named Bhadra,
Cetonuga, Kauśika, Kāla, Viśva, Suśiva, and another, Kopa.

33.s:
śrutyagnyare syurete strīpāṭhācchaktayastvetāḥ /
juṃkāro'thāgnipatnīti ṣaḍare ṣaṇṭhavarjitāḥ // 17
33.d:
श्रुत्यग्न्यरे स्युरेते स्त्रीपाठाच्छक्तयस्त्वेताः ।
जुंकारोऽथाग्निपत्नीति षडरे षण्ठवर्जिताः ॥ 17
33.m:
These should be on the twelve-spoked [wheel]; but from their feminine reading, these are powers.
Then the syllable juṃ, and the wife of fire [svāhā]; in a six-spoked [wheel], they are devoid of the neuter [vowels].

33.s:
dvādaśāre tatsahitāḥ ṣoḍaśāre svarāḥ kramāt /
halastaddviguṇe'ṣṭāre yādyaṃ hāntaṃ tu tattrike // 18
33.d:
द्वादशारे तत्सहिताः षोडशारे स्वराः क्रमात् ।
हलस्तद्द्विगुणेऽष्टारे याद्यं हान्तं तु तत्त्रिके ॥ 18
33.m:
In a twelve-spoked [wheel], they include them; in a sixteen-spoked [wheel], the vowels in order;
in double that, the consonants; in an eight-spoked [wheel], [the letters] beginning with ya and ending with ha, but in its triad,

33.s:
dvātriṃśadarake sāntaṃ binduḥ sarveṣu mūrdhani /
evamanyānbahūṃścakrabhedānasmātprakalpayet // 19
33.d:
द्वात्रिंशदरके सान्तं बिन्दुः सर्वेषु मूर्धनि ।
एवमन्यान्बहूंश्चक्रभेदानस्मात्प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ 19
33.m:
in a thirty-two-spoked [wheel], [consonants] ending with sa; the bindu upon the crown of all of them.
In this way, one should fashion many other varieties of wheels from this [principle].

33.s:
eka eva cidātmaiṣa viśvāmarśanasārakaḥ /
śaktistadvānato mātā śabdarāśiḥ prakīrtitau // 20
33.d:
एक एव चिदात्मैष विश्वामर्शनसारकः ।
शक्तिस्तद्वानतो माता शब्दराशिः प्रकीर्तितौ ॥ 20
33.m:
This consciousness-self is single indeed, the essence of the reflective awareness of all.
Power and the possessor of power: hence the mother and the totality of sounds are proclaimed.

33.s:
tayoreva vibhāge tu śaktitadvatprakalpane /
śabdarāśirmālinī ca kṣobhātma vapurīdṛśam // 21
33.d:
तयोरेव विभागे तु शक्तितद्वत्प्रकल्पने ।
शब्दराशिर्मालिनी च क्षोभात्म वपुरीदृशम् ॥ 21
33.m:
When distinguishing between just those two, in conceiving power and the possessor of power,
[they are] the totality of sounds and Mālinī, such being their agitated nature.

33.s:
tathāntaḥsthaparāmarśabhedane vastutastrikam /
anuttarecchonmeṣākhyaṃ yato viśvaṃ vimarśanam // 22
33.d:
तथान्तःस्थपरामर्शभेदने वस्तुतस्त्रिकम् ।
अनुत्तरेच्छोन्मेषाख्यं यतो विश्वं विमर्शनम् ॥ 22
33.m:
Likewise, in dividing the inward reflective awareness, in reality there is a triad
called the unexcelled, will, and emergence, from which proceeds the reflective awareness of the universe.

33.s:
ānandeśormiyoge tu tatṣaṭkaṃ samudāhṛtam /
antaḥsthoṣmasamāyogāttadaṣṭakamudāhṛtam // 23
33.d:
आनन्देशोर्मियोगे तु तत्षट्कं समुदाहृतम् ।
अन्तःस्थोष्मसमायोगात्तदष्टकमुदाहृतम् ॥ 23
33.m:
Through connection with bliss, the sovereign ruler, and surging waves, it is declared as a hexad;
through union with the semivowels and sibilants, it is declared as an octad.

33.s:
tadāmṛtacatuṣkonabhāve dvādaśakaṃ bhavet /
tadyoge ṣoḍaśākhyaṃ syādevaṃ yāvadasaṃkhyatā // 24
33.d:
तदामृतचतुष्कोनभावे द्वादशकं भवेत् ।
तद्योगे षोडशाख्यं स्यादेवं यावदसंख्यता ॥ 24
33.m:
In the absence of that tetrad of immortal [neuters], it becomes a dodecad;
with their addition, it is called a hexadecad, and so on up to infinity.

33.s:
viśvamekaparāmarśasahatvātprabhṛti sphuṭam /
aṃśāṃśikāparāmarśān paryante sahate yataḥ // 25
33.d:
विश्वमेकपरामर्शसहत्वात्प्रभृति स्फुटम् ।
अंशांशिकापरामर्शान् पर्यन्ते सहते यतः ॥ 25
33.m:
For clearly the universe, beginning with the capacity for a single reflective awareness,
ultimately admits of reflective awarenesses of parts upon parts.

33.s:
ataḥ pañcāśadaikātmyaṃ svaravyaktivirūpatā /
vargāṣṭakaṃ varṇabheda ekāśītikalodayaḥ // 26
33.d:
अतः पञ्चाशदैकात्म्यं स्वरव्यक्तिविरूपता ।
वर्गाष्टकं वर्णभेद एकाशीतिकलोदयः ॥ 26
33.m:
Therefore, the identity of the fifty [letters], the manifold diversity of vowels and consonants,
the eight groups, the division of letters, [and] the emergence of eighty-one kalās,

33.s:
iti pradarśitaṃ pūrvam ardhamātrāsahatvataḥ /
svarārdhamapyasti yataḥ svaritasyārdhamātrakam // 27
33.d:
इति प्रदर्शितं पूर्वम् अर्धमात्रासहत्वतः ।
स्वरार्धमप्यस्ति यतः स्वरितस्यार्धमात्रकम् ॥ 27
33.m:
as demonstrated earlier, owing to its admitting half-measures;
for half a vowel also exists, since the circumflex vowel has half a mora.

33.s:
tasyādita udāttaṃ tatkathitaṃ padavedinā /
itthaṃ saṃvidiyaṃ yājyasvarūpāmarśarūpiṇī // 28
33.d:
तस्यादित उदात्तं तत्कथितं पदवेदिना ।
इत्थं संविदियं याज्यस्वरूपामर्शरूपिणी ॥ 28
33.m:
The acute [accent] at its beginning has been stated by the knower of words.
In this manner, this consciousness consists of the reflective awareness of the nature of the object of sacrifice.

33.s:
abhinnaṃ saṃvidaścaitaccakrāṇāṃ cakravālakam /
svāmyāvaraṇabhedena bahudhā tatprayojayet // 29
33.d:
अभिन्नं संविदश्चैतच्चक्राणां चक्रवालकम् ।
स्वाम्यावरणभेदेन बहुधा तत्प्रयोजयेत् ॥ 29
33.m:
And this circle of wheels is non-different from consciousness;
one should apply it in many ways according to the distinction of the sovereign [deity] and the surrounding deities.

33.s:
parāparā parā cānyā sṛṣṭisthititirodhayaḥ /
mātṛsadbhāvarūpā tu turyā viśrāntirucyate // 30
33.d:
परापरा परा चान्या सृष्टिस्थितितिरोधयः ।
मातृसद्भावरूपा तु तुर्या विश्रान्तिरुच्यते ॥ 30
33.m:
Higher-and-lower, higher, and the other: creation, stasis, and concealment;
and the fourth resting place, consisting of the essence of the cognising subject, is declared.

33.s:
tacca prakāśaṃ vaktrasthaṃ sūcitaṃ tu pade pade /
turye viśrāntirādheyā mātṛsadbhāvasāriṇi // 31
33.d:
तच्च प्रकाशं वक्त्रस्थं सूचितं तु पदे पदे ।
तुर्ये विश्रान्तिराधेया मातृसद्भावसारिणि ॥ 31
33.m:
And that luminosity located in the mouth has been indicated at every step;
rest is to be established in the fourth [state], which flows with the essence of the cognising subject.

33.s:
tathāsya viśvamābhāti svātmatanmayatāṃ gatam /
ityeṣa śāstrārthasyokta ekīkāro gurūditaḥ // 32
33.d:
तथास्य विश्वमाभाति स्वात्मतन्मयतां गतम् ।
इत्येष शास्त्रार्थस्योक्त एकीकारो गुरूदितः ॥ 32
33.m:
Thus the universe appears to him, having attained oneness with his own self.
Thus has been spoken this unification of the scripture's meaning, as taught by the guru.

34.s:
ucyate'tha svasvarūpapraveśaḥ kramasaṅgataḥ /
yadetadbahudhā proktamāṇavaṃ śivatāptaye /
tatrāntarantarāviśya viśrāmyetsavidhe pade // 1
34.d:
उच्यतेऽथ स्वस्वरूपप्रवेशः क्रमसङ्गतः ।
यदेतद्बहुधा प्रोक्तमाणवं शिवताप्तये ।
तत्रान्तरन्तराविश्य विश्राम्येत्सविधे पदे ॥ 1
34.m:
Now is explained entry into one's own essential nature through succession.
That which has been declared in many ways as pertaining to the individual self (āṇava) for the attainment of Śivahood—
penetrating into that between intervals, one should rest in the proximate abode.

Then, abandoning the individual state, one should resort to the plane of power (śākta);
then to the plane of Śambhu (śāmbhava), clearly by such a graded order of superiority.

34.s:
itthaṃ kramoditavibodhamahāmarīcisaṃpūritaprasarabhairavabhāvabhāgī /
ante'bhyupāyanirapekṣatayaiva nityaṃ svātmānamāviśati garbhitaviśvarūpam // 3
kathito'yaṃ svasvarūpapraveśaḥ parameṣṭhinā /
34.d:
इत्थं क्रमोदितविबोधमहामरीचिसंपूरितप्रसरभैरवभावभागी ।
अन्तेऽभ्युपायनिरपेक्षतयैव नित्यं स्वात्मानमाविशति गर्भितविश्वरूपम् ॥ 3
कथितोऽयं स्वस्वरूपप्रवेशः परमेष्ठिना ।
34.m:
Thus sharing in the Bhairava-state whose expanse is filled with the great rays of awakening arisen in succession,
in the end, independently of any means whatsoever, he eternally enters into his own self, which holds within it the form of the universe.
This entry into one's own essential nature has been declared by the Supreme Lord.
